questions.question: In the Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi-2at%O HEA system, does increasing the oxygen concentration beyond 2.0 at% further enhance the amplitude-independent damping peak height without reducing the ductility gained from ordered oxygen complexes?
questions.rationale: Answering this determines if the current 2.0 at% oxygen content is optimal or if higher interstitial loading is viable for further damping enhancement while maintaining the ductility benefit.
questions.decision_use: Optimizes interstitial doping levels to maximize damping capacity while retaining the unexpected ductility improvement observed in O-2 HEA.
answer_requirements: Measure damping capacity (tanδ) and tensile ductility (elongation) for Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi HEAs with oxygen concentrations of 2.5, 3.0, and 3.5 at%.
Compare peak heights of the low-temperature damping peak and total elongation against the 2.0 at% baseline.
evidence_spans: The addition of oxygen or nitrogen effectively further enhances the damping capacity
Particularly, the ductility of the O-2 HEA was unexpectedly doubled
~18.5% of all the oxygen atoms in the O-2 HEA participate in the formation of ordered oxygen complexes, enabling the enhanced ductility of this material
